source.publication: 2025 DR 0104 Booklet (Colorado Individual Income Tax), DR 0104 and DR 0104AD
source.section: DR 0104AD line 4 / line 6 Pension and Annuity Subtraction (PDF p.18-19 Line 4 bullets; p.19-20 Line 6; DR 0104AD p.1 lines 4 and 6), second bullet (at least 55, not yet 65); DR 0104 lines 1, 10-13 (PDF p.8, p.10); tax table PDF p.34-35

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (you) 50,000.00 + IRA distribution (you) 12,000.00 = 62,000.00. Federal taxable income = 62,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 46,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). DR 0104 line 1 federal taxable income (Form 1040 line 15) 46,250.00; lines 2-9 additions 0.00 (no state income tax addback, no other-state bond interest; federal AGI 62,000.00 is not over 300,000, so no line 4 deduction addback); line 10 subtotal 46,250.00. DR 0104AD: Line 4 (primary taxpayer, age 60, at least 55 but not yet 65): taxable pension, annuity and IRA income 12,000.00; limit 20,000.00 minus line 3 0.00 = 20,000.00; subtraction = smaller of 12,000.00 and 20,000.00 = 12,000.00. Line 22 subtotal = 12,000.00; DR 0104 line 11 = 12,000.00. Line 12 Colorado taxable income = 46,250.00 - 12,000.00 = 34,250.00. Line 13 tax = 4.4% x 34,250.00 = 1,507.00 (the tax table row over 34,200.00 but not over 34,300.00, PDF p.35, gives 1,507.00; expected keeps the formula figure). No credits claimed: 0.00. Colorado income tax 1,507.00.
accepted_approximations: Tax is figured on the exact income at 4.4%; below 50,000 the booklet uses the tax table, which taxes each 100-dollar row at its midpoint and rounds to the dollar.
